  247|       |/// Tier 4 click ΓåÆ checkbox-state toggle. Re-enabled after the
  248|       |/// egui 0.27 ΓåÆ 0.35 upgrade.
  249|       |///
  250|       |/// The checkbox widget reads/writes a `&mut bool` that lives
  251|       |/// in the test's render closure. With `Harness::new` that
  252|       |/// `bool` is re-initialized to its default every frame, so
  253|       |/// the visual state flickers back to unchecked on the settling
  254|       |/// frame after a click. The state-based capture pattern
  255|       |/// (capture the boolean *at the moment the click is processed*)
  256|       |/// is the only reliable way to assert the click handler fired
  257|       |/// and the state flipped. See the copy-code test for the same
  258|       |/// pattern.
  259|       |#[test]
  260|      1|fn test_task_checkbox_click_toggles_state() {
  261|       |    use accesskit::Role;
  262|       |    use egui_kittest::Harness;
  263|       |    use egui_kittest::kittest::Queryable;
  264|       |
  265|      1|    let mut harness = Harness::new_ui_state(
  266|      8|        |ui, captured: &mut Vec<bool>| {
  267|       |            // The renderer passes a local `checked: bool` into
  268|       |            // `ui.checkbox`. We mirror that here and snapshot
  269|       |            // the post-frame value into the harness state.
  270|      8|            let mut checked = false;
  271|      8|            let response = ui.checkbox(&mut checked, "todo");
  272|      8|            let _ = response; // silence unused warning if any
  273|      8|            captured.push(checked);
  274|      8|        },
  275|      1|        Vec::<bool>::new(),
  276|       |    );
  277|      1|    harness.fit_contents();
  278|      1|    harness.run();
  279|       |
  280|       |    // Locate the checkbox by role and click. `step()` processes
  281|       |    // the queued hover/press/release events in one go.
  282|      1|    let checkbox = harness.get_by_role(Role::CheckBox);
  283|      1|    checkbox.click();
  284|      1|    harness.step();
  285|       |
  286|       |    // The captured vector accumulates one entry per frame; what
  287|       |    // matters is that the *post-click* frame flipped the local
  288|       |    // `checked` to `true`. If the click handler did not fire,
  289|       |    // the last entry would still be `false` (the closure would
  290|       |    // re-initialize `checked` from scratch with no events to
  291|       |    // consume).
  292|      1|    let captured = harness.state();
  293|      1|    assert_eq!(
  294|      1|        captured.last().copied(),
  295|       |        Some(true),
  296|       |        "clicking an unchecked task-list checkbox must flip the local `checked` value to `true`; \
  297|       |         captured sequence: {captured:?}"
  298|       |    );
  299|       |    // Pre-click frames should all be `false` (no widget state
  300|       |    // to persist across frames in the local `checked`).
  301|      1|    assert!(
  302|      1|        captured.iter().any(|&v| v),
  303|       |        "at least one captured value must be `true` (the post-click frame); got {captured:?}"
  304|       |    );
  305|      1|}

    3|       |//! Covers:

    1|       |//! Off-viewport guards + table row-geometry regressions.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! Covers the catch-all table regressions that don't fit the
    4|       |//! column-alignment, FTWA, or interaction submodules:
    5|       |//!
    6|       |//! - Off-viewport text guards at narrow (┬º3.6 fallback) and wide
    7|       |//!   (FTWA) viewports (MD-013).
    8|       |//! - Multi-frame row-height stability (no per-frame oscillation).
    9|       |//! - Empty cells not inflating `row_max_h` (the phantom-row-height
   10|       |//!   regression from `2022 sports car.md`).
   11|       |//! - Single-line cell text top-aligned in a row with a multi-line
   12|       |//!   neighbor (TBL-031 / `top_down` layout fix) ΓÇö exercised via
   13|       |//!   the 2-pass `render_table_with_config` path. The other
   14|       |//!   top-alignment tests (1-pass `render_table`, 1-pass
   15|       |//!   `render_markdown`) live in `table_alignment.rs` and
   16|       |//!   `tests/table_visual_layout_test.rs` respectively.
   17|       |
   18|       |use super::*;
   19|       |
   20|       |// ---- Off-viewport text guards (MD-013) -------------------------
   21|       |
   22|       |/// Render the long-table-row fixture and assert no `Shape::Text`
   23|       |/// is permanently outside its containing clip rect. Catches the
   24|       |/// F1 (horizontal clip) and F3 (table column overflow) failure
   25|       |/// modes; the ┬º3.6 fallback in `render_table` must wrap the
   26|       |/// table in a horizontal `ScrollArea` so cell text remains
   27|       |/// reachable.
   28|       |///
   29|       |/// Mirrors the production render path: `render_markdown` is
   30|       |/// always wrapped in a vertical `ScrollArea` by the center panel
   31|       |/// (`src/ui/panels/center.rs:364`). The test must do the same,
   32|       |/// otherwise tall content trivially exceeds the viewport's
   33|       |/// bottom edge and triggers a false positive.
   34|       |///
   35|       |/// Consolidated from two formerly-separate tests
   36|       |/// (`render_markdown_no_offscreen_text_at_narrow_viewport` and
   37|       |/// `..._at_wide_viewport`) ΓÇö they were 95% identical, differing
   38|       |/// only in `viewport_width`. The narrow case exercises the ┬º3.6
   39|       |/// fallback (table wider than viewport); the wide case exercises

C:\Users\mkuhn\src\ppai\src\desktop\src\ui\render\table\cell.rs:
    1|       |//! Single-cell rendering for markdown tables.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! When `pinned_width` is `Some(w)`, the cell Ui is clamped to exactly `w`
    4|       |//! pixels (`ui.set_width`) and text is laid out with `horizontal_wrapped` +
    5|       |//! `Label::wrap(true)` so that multi-word cells wrap at whitespace. This is the
    6|       |//! FTWA-pinned mode (`crate::ui::table_width`). The FTWA invariant
    7|       |//! `w >= min_content >= longest-token` guarantees no unbreakable token is ever
    8|       |//! split or clipped ΓÇö only inter-word whitespace wraps.
    9|       |//!
   10|       |//! When `pinned_width` is `None` (the ┬º3.6 fallback path), the cell uses
   11|       |//! `ui.horizontal` (no wrap) so the cell reports its full single-line intrinsic
   12|       |//! width to the parent table layout; any overflow is handled by the wrapping
   13|       |//! `ScrollArea` (current pre-FTWA behaviour).
   14|       |//!
   15|       |//! **Padding (TBL-032, TBL-033):** `padding` is resolved per-cell by the caller
   16|       |//! via `resolve_padding(global, per_column, per_cell)` and applied as the
   17|       |//! cell frame's `inner_margin`. `padding.horizontal()` is folded into the
   18|       |//! column's `max_content`/`min_content` by `measure_cached`, so the FTWA-assigned
   19|       |//! `pinned_width` already accounts for it; the inner layout width is therefore
   20|       |//! `pinned_width - padding.horizontal()` so text fits inside the padded frame.
   21|       |//!
   22|       |//! **Multi-element cells:** Cells with multiple `InlineElem` entries
   23|       |//! (e.g. `~~strikethrough~~ **bold**` parsed as `[Text(strikethrough), Text(" "), Text(bold)]`)
   24|       |//! are rendered as a single inline `LayoutJob` rather than as vertically-
   25|       |//! stacked labels. Stacking the elements as separate `Label` widgets under
   26|       |//! `top_down` made the cell as wide as the *widest single token* of any
   27|       |//! element (e.g. `$180ΓÇô$210` at ~107 px) and ignored `set_max_width(inner_w)`,
   28|       |//! because a single `Label` with no whitespace in its text cannot wrap and
   29|       |//! the placer reports the label's natural width ΓÇö which then overflowed the
   30|       |//! column by ~10 px and pushed every subsequent cell in the same row right
   31|       |//! by the same amount. Inline `LayoutJob` rendering makes the entire cell
   32|       |//! content flow as a single wrapped line within `inner_w`, matching the
   33|       |//! "one styled run after another, wrap at whitespace" semantic the
   34|       |//! cell measurer already assumes when it sums per-element widths into
   35|       |//! `max_content`. Cells that contain non-text elements (`Link`, `Image`,
   36|       |//! `Html`) fall back to the per-element rendering ΓÇö they cannot be
   37|       |//! represented as `TextFormat` runs in a `LayoutJob`.
   38|       |
   39|       |use crate::markdown::InlineElem;
   40|       |use crate::ui::table_width::TablePadding;
   41|       |use eframe::egui;
   42|       |use egui::RichText;
   43|       |use egui::epaint::text::{LayoutJob, TextWrapping};
   44|       |
   45|       |/// Purpose: Renders a single table cell, always emitting at least one widget.

   55|  8.41k|    let pad_v = pad.vertical();

   57|       |    // representable range after rounding. Realistic paddings are small

   59|       |    // practice and keeps `Margin`'s compact layout intact.
   60|  33.6k|    let to_i8 = |v: f32| -> i8 { v.round().clamp(0.0, 127.0) as i8 };

    1|       |//! Markdown table rendering with a [`TableRenderConfig`].
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! Per-column pixel widths are computed by `crate::ui::table_width::ftwa`
    4|       |//! from egui-shaped max-content and min-content measurements; cells are
    5|       |//! then pinned to their assigned width so the child Ui's available_width
    6|       |//! matches the column width (see
    7|       |//! `doc/planning/table-column-width-algorithm.md` ┬º5 decision Q5). When
    8|       |//! the available width falls below the sum of min-content
    9|       |//! (`decision.needs_horizontal_scroll`), the table physically cannot fit
   10|       |//! even with every column at its longest-token floor and we fall back to
   11|       |//! the prior behaviour: a wrapping `ScrollArea` over max-content columns
   12|       |//! (doc ┬º3.6) so the strongest invariant ΓÇö never split a token ΓÇö is
   13|       |//! preserved. The horizontal scrollbar is forced visible in that path
   14|       |//! so the overflow is discoverable instead of looking like a silently-
   15|       |//! clipped rightmost cell.
   16|       |//!
   17|       |//! Column spacing is 10.0 px and row spacing is 4.0 px. The available content
   18|       |//! width passed to FTWA subtracts `(N - 1) * 10.0` for those gutters so the
   19|       |//! assigned widths sum to the true content rect.
   20|       |//!
   21|       |//! The whole table ΓÇö both the FTWA path and the ┬º3.6 horizontal-scroll
   22|       |//! fallback ΓÇö is wrapped in a `Frame::NONE.stroke(TABLE_PERIMETER_STROKE)`
   23|       |//! (medium gray, 1 px) so the table reads as a single bordered block on
   24|       |//! screen.

    1|       |//! Fair Table Width Algorithm (FTWA) ΓÇö assigns per-column pixel widths to a markdown/GFM table.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! Reconciles two goals (see `doc/planning/table-column-width-algorithm.md`):
    4|       |//!   **G1** minimize total word-wrap (extra wrapped lines) and
    5|       |//!   **G3** use all available horizontal space.
    6|       |//!
    7|       |//! G2 ("minimize the number of columns that wrap") is no longer a goal: every
    8|       |//! positive-slack column can participate in shrinking the deficit, and B2
    9|       |//! distributes the deficit across all of them.
   10|       |//!
   11|       |//! Pure `ftwa` core lives in `crate::markdown::table_width` (pure layout math,
   12|       |//! per `src/desktop/AGENTS.md ┬º5`); this module bridges to egui text shaping via
   13|       |//! `measure` / `measure_cached` / `ftwa_cached` and re-exports the pure API so
   14|       |//! existing call sites (`crate::ui::table_width::ftwa_cached`) keep resolving

C:\Users\mkuhn\src\ppai\src\desktop\src\ui\test_helpers\assert.rs:
    1|       |//! Id-stability test pattern helpers.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! # Why this exists
    4|       |//!
    5|       |//! The most common egui bug class in this project is the
    6|       |//! `WARN egui::context: Widget rect ... changed id between passes`
    7|       |//! warning. The AGENTS.md ┬º"Conditional rendering" section documents the
    8|       |//! root cause and the fix (always allocate, toggle visibility with
    9|       |//! `add_visible` / `set_invisible`). Until a test exists for a panel,
   10|       |//! the warning can be reintroduced by a well-meaning refactor that wraps
   11|       |//! a panel in `if cond { Panel::right("...").show(...) }` and the `if`
   12|       |//! arm's allocation shape changes between passes.
   13|       |//!
   14|       |//! # Two complementary detection mechanisms
   15|       |//!
   16|       |//! Both are needed because they can fail independently:
   17|       |//!
   18|       |//! 1. **Red-stroke shape detection** ΓÇö egui's
   19|       |//!    `Context::warn_if_rect_changes_id` draws a red `Shape::Rect` outline
   20|       |//!    in the second pass when it detects the warning. The test renders
   21|       |//!    the panel twice (priming the first-pass state, then observing the
   22|       |//!    second pass), walks `output.shapes`, and asserts no shape has
   23|       |//!    `stroke.color == Color32::RED`.
   24|       |//!
   25|       |//! 2. **Log capture** ΓÇö egui emits the warning to the `log` crate. A test
   26|       |//!    can install a `log::Log` impl, render across a bool flip, and
   27|       |//!    grep the captured messages.
   28|       |//!
   29|       |//! The red-stroke mechanism can be suppressed by `ctx.set_theme(Light)`
   30|       |//! (the warning's red debug colour is hidden against certain
   31|       |//! backgrounds), and the log-capture mechanism can be lost if the test
   32|       |//! process has another `log::set_logger` installed. Belt-and-suspenders.
   33|       |//!
   34|       |//! # Existing test sites
   35|       |//!
   36|       |//! - `panels/top.rs:289` ΓÇö log capture, covers the `indexing_finished`
   37|       |//!   bool flip on the toolbar.
   38|       |//! - `panels/left.rs:451` ΓÇö red-stroke, covers the file tree, empty
   39|       |//!   state, transition, and width-clamping.
   40|       |//! - `ui/app.rs:1352` ΓÇö red-stroke, covers the full 5-panel render with
   41|       |//!   TOC active.
   42|       |//!
   43|       |//! # Usage
   44|       |//!
   45|       |//! ```ignore
   46|       |//! use crate::ui::test_helpers::assert::assert_no_id_change_warnings;
   47|       |//!
   48|       |//! // Install log capture (one-time, guarded by OnceLock<()>).
   49|       |//! // ... (see panels/top.rs:289-360 for the full pattern)
   50|       |//!

    1|       |//! Tier 4 interaction test helpers ΓÇö the state-capture pattern.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! # Why this exists
    4|       |//!
    5|       |//! egui 0.35 replaced `PlatformOutput::copied_text` / `open_url` with
    6|       |//! `PlatformOutput::commands: Vec<OutputCommand>`. Worse, `PlatformOutput`
    7|       |//! is now per-frame ΓÇö every new pass starts a fresh `PlatformOutput`.
    8|       |//! A click that emits `OutputCommand::CopyText(text)` on frame N has that
    9|       |//! command **overwritten on frame N+1**, before the test can read it.
   10|       |//!
   11|       |//! This is the opposite of what `Harness::output()` would suggest. The
   12|       |//! naive pattern ΓÇö "render, click, render, assert on
   13|       |//! `harness.output().platform_output.commands`" ΓÇö silently fails because
   14|       |//! the `run()`-and-settle cycle has already started a new pass and erased
   15|       |//! the click's output.
   16|       |//!
   17|       |//! # The fix
   18|       |//!
   19|       |//! Capture the click's side effect into the harness's **persistent state**
   20|       |//! at the moment it fires. The harness's `state()` is preserved across
   21|       |//! frames; the closure's `T` argument is the same `T` for every frame.
   22|       |//! Push the side effect onto a `Vec` (or set a `bool`, or write a
   23|       |//! `String`) inside that state, then read `harness.state()` after
   24|       |//! `harness.step()` to see what fired.
   25|       |//!
   26|       |//! # Canonical example
   27|       |//!
   28|       |//! ```ignore
   29|       |//! use crate::ui::test_helpers::interact::stateful_harness;
   30|       |//!
   31|       |//! let mut harness = stateful_harness(Vec::<String>::new(), |ui, captured| {
   32|       |//!     if ui.button("Copy").clicked() {
   33|       |//!         ui.copy_text("let x = 1;".to_string());
   34|       |//!         captured.push("let x = 1;".to_string());
   35|       |//!     }
   36|       |//! });
   37|       |//! harness.fit_contents();
   38|       |//! harness.run();
   39|       |//! harness.get_by_label("Copy").click();
   40|       |//! // Two runs after the click: the first processes pointer events
   41|       |//! // (hover + press + release = three steps), the second settles
   42|       |//! // any post-click repaint.
   43|       |//! harness.run();
   44|       |//! harness.run();
   45|       |//! let captured = harness.state();
   46|       |//! assert_eq!(captured, vec!["let x = 1;".to_string()]);
   47|       |//! ```
   48|       |//!
   49|       |//! Real example: `src/ui/render.rs::test_copy_code_button_click_copies_to_output`.
   50|       |//!
   51|       |//! # When *not* to use state-capture
   52|       |//!
   53|       |//! When the side effect lives only in `PlatformOutput::commands` and
   54|       |//! cannot be intercepted at the closure level (e.g. `OpenUrl` from a
   55|       |//! `Link` widget), the alternative is to use `harness.step()` (not
   56|       |//! `run()`) to drive the click and read `harness.output()` in the narrow
   57|       |//! window before the next frame overwrites the command. See
   58|       |//! `src/ui/render.rs::test_hyperlink_click_opens_url` for the pattern.
   59|       |
   60|       |/// Build a stateful egui_kittest `Harness` for a Tier 4 click test.
   61|       |///
   62|       |/// The closure receives `&mut egui::Ui` and `&mut T`. `T` is the
   63|       |/// persistent state and is re-used across frames (measure, paint, click,
   64|       |/// repaint). The closure is re-invoked for each pass ΓÇö push the click's
   65|       |/// side effect into `T`, then assert on `harness.state()` after the
   66|       |/// click has settled.
   67|       |///
   68|       |/// This is a thin alias for `egui_kittest::Harness::new_ui_state`. It
   69|       |/// exists to give the pattern a project-specific name and a doc-comment
   70|       |/// anchor; the harness API itself is unchanged.
   71|       |///
   72|       |/// The lifetime parameter `'a` ties the harness to the closure's borrow
   73|       |/// lifetime. In practice, this is the lifetime of the test function ΓÇö
   74|       |/// the closure is non-`'static` and the harness borrows from it.
   75|     13|pub fn stateful_harness<'a, T, F>(initial_state: T, body: F) -> egui_kittest::Harness<'a, T>
   76|     13|where
   77|     13|    T: 'static,
   78|     13|    F: FnMut(&mut eframe::egui::Ui, &mut T) + 'a,
   79|       |{
   80|     13|    egui_kittest::Harness::new_ui_state(body, initial_state)
   81|     13|}

    1|       |//! Off-viewport / off-screen text rendering guards.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! Walks the rendered shape list from an `egui::Context::run_ui` call and
    4|       |//! asserts that every text shape is reachable in the user's viewport ΓÇö
    5|       |//! its painted rect is inside its containing `ClippedShape.clip_rect`.
    6|       |//! Catches the F1 (horizontal clip), F6 (zero / negative / transformed
    7|       |//! off-screen), and F7 (zero-rect allocation) classes from
    8|       |//! `doc/planning/off-viewport-text-strategy.md` ┬º"Failure-mode taxonomy".
    9|       |//!
   10|       |//! # Why a separate helper
   11|       |//!
   12|       |//! `text::assert_text_contains` only checks text content. The id-stability
   13|       |//! helper (`assert::assert_no_id_change_warnings`) only catches the
   14|       |//! pass-to-pass shape change bug class. Neither covers "the text is
   15|       |//! rendered, but in a rect the user cannot see or scroll to". This
   16|       |//! module fills that gap.
   17|       |//!
   18|       |//! # Usage
   19|       |//!
   20|       |//! ```ignore
   21|       |//! use crate::ui::test_helpers::offscreen::assert_no_offscreen_text;
   22|       |//!
   23|       |//! let output = ctx.run_ui(raw_input, |ui| {
   24|       |//!     render_markdown(&doc, ...);
   25|       |//! });
   26|       |//! assert_no_offscreen_text(&output.shapes);
   27|       |//! ```
   28|       |//!
   29|       |//! # Reachability contract
   30|       |//!
   31|       |//! A text shape is considered **reachable** when:
   32|       |//!
   33|       |//! 1. Its visual bounding rect (`Shape::visual_bounding_rect`) has
   34|       |//!    positive area on both axes, AND
   35|       |//! 2. Its containing `ClippedShape.clip_rect` has positive area, AND
   36|       |//! 3. The text visual rect intersects the clip rect (so at least
   37|       |//!    some pixels of the text are visible inside the clip).
   38|       |//!
   39|       |//! When condition 3 fails the text is fully clipped; we report both
   40|       |//! rects so the diagnostic is actionable. When condition 1 or 2 fails
   41|       |//! the shape has a degenerate allocation ΓÇö F6 / F7 territory.
   42|       |
   43|       |use eframe::egui;
   44|       |
   45|       |/// One concrete off-viewport text shape violation found by
   46|       |/// [`find_offscreen_text`].

   49|       |    /// First non-empty line of the rendered text (clipped for the message).

   52|       |    pub text_rect: egui::Rect,
   53|       |    /// The clip rect the shape was placed in. `None` when the shape
   54|       |    /// carries no clip rect (should not happen for text in egui 0.35,
   55|       |    /// but flagged when it does).
   56|       |    pub clip_rect: Option<egui::Rect>,
   57|       |    /// Why the shape was rejected.
   58|       |    pub reason: OffscreenReason,
   59|       |}

C:\Users\mkuhn\src\ppai\src\desktop\src\ui\test_helpers\snapshot.rs:
    1|       |//! Tier 3 visual regression snapshot helpers.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! Wraps the `egui_kittest` snapshot API with project-standard options:
    4|       |//! 3px per-channel pixel diff threshold (Q10), `tests/snapshots/`
    5|       |//! output path, and a builder that wires up a known viewport.
    6|       |//!
    7|       |//! # Why this exists
    8|       |//!
    9|       |//! Per the R-1 deliverable in `doc/planning/egui-testing.md`, the
   10|       |//! project's most complex visual surface (the markdown renderer) has
   11|       |//! no visual regression coverage. A real refactor that changes a
   12|       |//! column's wrap point, a heading's left padding, or a code block's
   13|       |//! border thickness would pass the current test suite silently.
   14|       |//! Snapshots close that gap.
   15|       |//!
   16|       |//! # Usage
   17|       |//!
   18|       |//! ```ignore
   19|       |//! use crate::ui::test_helpers::snapshot::snapshot_harness;
   20|       |//!
   21|       |//! let mut harness = snapshot_harness("ftwa_6col_table", egui::vec2(1200.0, 600.0), |ui| {
   22|       |//!     let table = build_six_col_table();
   23|       |//!     fastmd::ui::render::render_table(ui, &table, 0, fastmd::ui::table_width::DeficitStrategy::ProportionalToSlack);
   24|       |//! });
   25|       |//! harness.run();
   26|       |//! harness.snapshot("ftwa_6col_table");
   27|       |//! ```
   28|       |//!
   29|       |//! # Q10 ΓÇö 3px project-wide threshold
   30|       |//!
   31|       |//! The threshold is set per-harness via `SnapshotOptions::threshold`.
   32|       |//! 3px was chosen over the original Q2 commitment of 5px because it
   33|       |//! catches a single line of text wrap (~14-16px) while still tolerating
   34|       |//! system-font metric variation across Windows / Linux CI / macOS.
   35|       |//!
   36|       |//! # Renderer requirement
   37|       |//!
   38|       |//! `egui_kittest`'s snapshot API requires a real renderer (the
   39|       |//! default `LazyRenderer` errors with "no default renderer
   40|       |//! available"). The `wgpu` feature on `egui_kittest` provides
   41|       |//! `WgpuTestRenderer`, which is the project's planned renderer. As
   42|       |//! of the 2026-07-27 branch, the `wgpu` feature is **not enabled**
   43|       |//! because pulling it in on Windows produces a wgpu-hal 0.29 /
   44|       |//! windows-core 0.56/0.62 trait-bound conflict that the local
   45|       |//! environment cannot compile. This is a separate, pre-existing
   46|       |//! issue in the wgpu / windows-core dependency graph; resolving it
   47|       |//! is out of scope for R-1. Once the wgpu dep conflict is sorted,
   48|       |//! callers should add `.wgpu()` to the `HarnessBuilder` chain in
   49|       |//! `snapshot_harness` below.
   50|       |//!
   51|       |//! Until the wgpu story is resolved, calling `harness.snapshot()`
   52|       |//! on this project will return `SnapshotError::RenderError` with a
   53|       |//! "no default renderer" message. The helper still exercises the
   54|       |//! full API surface; only the actual image write is blocked.
   55|       |//!
   56|       |//! # Real example: see `tests/render_snapshots.rs`
   57|       |//!
   58|       |//! That integration test takes 2-3 initial snapshots once the
   59|       |//! renderer is wired up.
   60|       |
   61|       |use eframe::egui;
   62|       |

   65|       |/// enabled on `egui_kittest`).

   10|       |/// Purpose: Applies the side effect of clicking a file row in the
   11|       |/// left panel's tree view.
   12|       |/// Inputs: ctx (the `TreeNodeContext`; its `selected_file`,
   13|       |/// `selected_files`, and `tabs` are mutated), row (the clicked
   14|       |/// `FlatRow`)
   15|       |/// Outputs: ()
   16|       |/// Purity: Impure (mutates the selection and tab state).
   17|       |/// Preconditions: `row.is_dir` should be `false` (caller filters
   18|       |/// files vs directories). Modifiers are taken from `ctx.modifiers()`
   19|       |/// at the moment of the call.
   20|       |/// Postconditions:
   21|       |///   * With any of shift/ctrl/command held: toggles the row's
   22|       |///     inclusion in `ctx.selected_files()`. If it was already in
   23|       |///     the set, it is removed and `ctx.selected_file()` is cleared
   24|       |///     if it pointed at this path. If it was not, it is added and
   25|       |///     `ctx.selected_file()` is set to it.
   26|       |///   * With no modifier: replaces the selection with this single
   27|       |///     file and pushes it onto `ctx.tabs()` if not already open.
   28|       |///   * **Always:** updates `ctx.selected_dir()` (the "current
   29|       |///     directory context" used by the bottom-panel prompt prefix
   30|       |///     and by the agent session dispatch) to the file's

   79|       |/// which only finds `.exe` (or extension-less) files while searching
   80|       |/// `PATH`. It cannot find the `.cmd` / `.bat` shims that toolchains

   82|       |/// `Command::new("npx")` fails with "program not found". This helper
   83|       |/// reproduces `cmd.exe`'s resolution: it scans every `PATH` directory
   84|       |/// for the command with each extension from `PATHEXT` (defaulting to
   85|       |/// `.COM;.EXE;.BAT;.CMD`) and returns the first match as an absolute
   86|       |/// path.

   89|       |/// passed through unchanged, as are commands that resolve to nothing
   90|       |/// (the caller then surfaces the original spawn error). On non-Windows
   91|       |/// platforms the input is returned unchanged.
